title: The depth of the mystery: divinity and flesh distinct yet one
english: Listen, then, to what I also have to say to you. Understand, my friend, the depth of the mystery, and go straight toward the goal of the sacred writings. For divinity and flesh, that is, humanity, are different realities, at least as far as concerns the accounts that apply to the properties present in both. For how, I ask, did he become as we are, when the Word, being God, had remained what he was?

orientation: Cyril opens his third book against Theodore by urging him to grasp the depth of the mystery of Christ, insisting that divinity and flesh are distinct in their natural properties yet must be confessed as one Son.
